Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0020", "row_sha256": "64659331e2c3c42c7b477484792ec2ad1468fd6d9d694f539310274c623f896e", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
lower case as this is still my working note. can you turn this into a self-contained ordinary update about registration for the fictional harbor city open chess tournament, not a tournament announcement and not a report on games. it should read like a practical update for players and families who have already heard of the event. keep it in English and make the facts easy to follow, but don't make it sound like a press release. i need the details below included, with the current registration picture kept separate from anything that is not known yet.

the tournament is scheduled for saturday, october 18, at the east pier community hall, with check-in from 8:15 to 8:50 in the morning and the first round planned for 9:15. the hall entrance is on alder street, not the waterfront side, which has a locked service door. people can use the municipal lot on alder after 8:00; the first two hours are free, and the posted rate applies after that. the bus stop is the one called pier market, a short walk from the entrance. the event is open to players in the open section and the under-14 section, and those are the only two sections currently listed. say that clearly rather than implying there is a separate beginner bracket. registration is being handled through the club's online form, with paper copies available at the library desk on weekday afternoons.

for the figures, as of monday at 6 pm, the club has 58 confirmed entries, 11 submitted forms that still need a correction, and six entries with fee status still pending. don't add those three groups together and call the result confirmed, and don't present the correction forms as rejected. confirmed entries are split as 41 in open and 17 under-14. the correction forms are eight open and three under-14, while the six pending-fee entries are four open and two under-14. the online list is refreshed each evening, but these counts are the monday snapshot, not a promise that it has already changed since then. there are 72 places in the playing hall, and the club is not saying that registration is closed or that any section is full. if a player submits a form but does not get the confirmation email, ask them to check spam and then contact the registrar; don't tell them to submit a second form straight away.

include the price and what it covers in a straightforward way. entry is $24 for open and $18 for under-14, payable by card in the online form or by cash at the library desk when leaving a paper form. the fee includes a sandwich lunch and a drink. a player who needs to cancel should email the registrar by october 12 for a refund; after that date the fee is not refundable. don't turn that into a claim about exceptions, because none are set out here. players may request one half-point bye, but the request has to arrive by october 12 and it is not automatic: the director reviews requests. a bye request doesn't reserve a place or change whether the registration form is complete. i'm not sure if we need all these practical details in a single flowing update, but do include the deadline and the distinction between asking and being granted one.

there is a volunteer check-in table at the alder street entrance, and the club will have printed section lists there. players should bring a chess set only if they already have one; the club has sets available, so don't make equipment a registration requirement. clocks are supplied by the organizers. the hall has step-free entry through the main alder street door and an accessible washroom on the ground floor. anyone needing a reserved space beside the hall should email the venue directly, since the club cannot reserve municipal parking spaces. the lunch is included for registered players, but the note from the caterer says dietary details should be sent to the registrar by october 10. don't suggest the menu or promise a particular substitute; those details are not settled in this note.

some people have asked whether they can register on the day. right now the club's plan is to accept walk-ins only if places remain after the online and paper forms have been checked, and the director will decide at the venue. don't write that walk-in entry is guaranteed or say that the club has decided against it either. the online registration deadline is october 15 at 7 pm, unless all 72 hall places are taken earlier; if that happens the club will post that registration has closed. paper forms must reach the library desk by closing time on october 14 so they can be entered before the online deadline. for a form correction, the registrar will email the player with the item to fix. if the corrected form comes in by october 15 at 7 pm, it can still be considered with the other entries, but do not promise confirmation before the deadline.

please use this exact quote from the club coordinator in an ordinary reported way: “We want the check-in line to move steadily, so please have your name and section ready when you reach the table.” don't turn it into a slogan or claim that the line will be short. i'd like a numbered part if it fits naturally, perhaps a small section showing the three current record statuses, but don't make up a fourth status or combine pending items with confirmed players. the update should have connected paragraphs, some concrete information throughout rather than a block of generic advice, and a clear last section. this is not meant to be a list of every possible tournament rule, and nothing here gives pairing details, round times after the first round, prizes, or results, so don't fill those gaps.

end with the current assessment, not a recap that claims everything is ready. the registration picture is usable but incomplete: 58 entries are confirmed, 11 forms need correction, and six fee statuses are pending, against 72 places in the hall. if all corrections and payments are received by the stated deadline, those entries can be reviewed with the rest; that condition does not make them confirmed now. the counts describe registration only, as of monday at 6 pm. keep the assessment limited to the registration record and available places; it does not establish event readiness, final attendance, pairings, or likely results. make this a distinct final paragraph and keep all of those limits and conditions in it.", "output": "Draft a self-contained, practical English update for players and families about registration for the fictional Harbor City Open chess tournament. This is an update for people who already know about the event, not a tournament announcement or a report on games. Use an ordinary, clear tone rather than sounding like a press release. Keep current registration information distinct from matters that are not yet known, and do not fill in missing tournament details.

The tournament is scheduled for Saturday, October 18, at East Pier Community Hall. Check-in is from 8:15 to 8:50 a.m., and the first round is planned for 9:15. The hall entrance is on Alder Street; the waterfront-side entrance is a locked service door. The municipal lot on Alder may be used after 8:00 a.m. The first two hours are free, and the posted rate applies after that. The nearby bus stop is Pier Market, a short walk from the entrance. The event currently lists only two sections: Open and Under-14. Do not imply that there is a separate beginner bracket. Registration is through the club’s online form, with paper copies available at the library desk on weekday afternoons.

For the registration figures, use the Monday, 6 p.m. snapshot: 58 confirmed entries, 11 submitted forms needing correction, and six entries with fee status pending. Confirmed entries comprise 41 Open and 17 Under-14 players. Of the forms needing correction, eight are Open and three Under-14; of the pending-fee entries, four are Open and two Under-14. Do not add these groups together and call the total confirmed, or describe forms needing correction as rejected. The online list is refreshed each evening, but the Monday figures are a snapshot, not a claim that it has changed since then. The playing hall has 72 places. The club has not said registration is closed or that a section is full.

Explain that if a player submits a form but does not receive a confirmation email, they should check their spam folder and then contact the registrar; do not advise them to submit a second form immediately. Entry costs $24 for Open and $18 for Under-14. Players may pay by card in the online form or in cash at the library desk when leaving a paper form. The fee includes a sandwich lunch and a drink. Players seeking a refund must email the registrar by October 12 to cancel; after that date, the fee is not refundable. Do not add exceptions that are not specified. Players may request one half-point bye by October 12, but the request is not automatic and is reviewed by the director. A bye request does not reserve a place or change whether a registration form is complete. Preserve the distinction between requesting a bye and receiving one.

Include the practical arrangements at the venue. A volunteer check-in table and printed section lists will be at the Alder Street entrance. Players may bring a chess set if they already have one, but the club has sets available, so a set is not a registration requirement. Organizers supply clocks. The main Alder Street door has step-free entry, and there is an accessible washroom on the ground floor. Anyone needing a reserved space beside the hall should email the venue directly; the club cannot reserve municipal parking spaces. Lunch is included for registered players. Dietary details should be sent to the registrar by October 10, as requested in the caterer’s note. Do not specify a menu or promise a substitute, since neither is settled here.

Clarify the deadlines and the status of walk-in registration. The online registration deadline is October 15 at 7 p.m., unless all 72 hall places are taken earlier. If all places are taken, the club will post that registration has closed. Paper forms must reach the library desk by closing time on October 14 so they can be entered before the online deadline. For a form correction, the registrar will email the player with the item to fix. If the corrected form arrives by October 15 at 7 p.m., it can still be considered with the other entries; do not promise confirmation before the deadline. The club currently plans to accept walk-ins only if places remain after online and paper forms have been checked, with the director deciding at the venue. Do not say walk-in entry is guaranteed or that the club has ruled it out.

Use this exact quote in ordinary reported speech: “We want the check-in line to move steadily, so please have your name and section ready when you reach the table.” Do not turn it into a slogan or claim the line will be short. A numbered section may be used naturally to show the three current record statuses, but do not create another status or combine pending items with confirmed players. Use connected paragraphs with concrete information throughout and a clear final section. This is not a list of every possible tournament rule. Do not invent pairing information, round times after the first round, prizes, or results.

End with a distinct final paragraph assessing registration, not a recap claiming that everything is ready. State that the registration picture is usable but incomplete: 58 entries are confirmed, 11 forms need correction, and six fee statuses are pending, against 72 places in the hall. If all corrections and payments are received by the stated deadline, those entries can be reviewed with the rest; that condition does not make them confirmed now. Limit the assessment to the registration record and available places, as of Monday at 6 p.m. It does not establish event readiness, final attendance, pairings, or likely results."}]
